steps.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)

evidence: Directly changes LICM's MemorySSA-based conflict scan and permits additional memory-def hoists.
Moving a MemoryDef while preserving loop MemorySSA is a strong match for an assertion about removing an access that still has uses.
features: licm-hoisting, memorydef-dominance, memoryssa-direct-use, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar, path:llvm/test/Analysis/MemorySSA
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The candidate changes LICM's MemorySSA-based hoist-safety analysis in noConflictingReadWrites: while checking a non-sink operation, it now skips a candidate memory access when the instruction's defining MemorySSA access dominates that candidate. New and updated LICM tests exercise hoisting of inaccessible-memory calls and changed promotion output, directly covering memory-effect ordering decisions made with loop MemorySSA.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA; LICMPass; LNICMPass; loop_alias; ne_loop_alias; fn_write_inaccessible_mem; fn_read_inaccessible_mem
Behavioral change: For non-sinking LICM queries, noConflictingReadWrites now ignores an access MA if MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA) is true.; This can permit hoisting by treating dominated MemorySSA accesses as non-conflicting for the relevant safety check.; The new loop-mssa LICM test expects a write to inaccessible memory to hoist when no conflicting inaccessible-memory read exists, and to remain in the loop when such a conflicting read is present.; Updated promotion checks show LICM retaining/loading through g_116 rather than using the prior direct promoted load from g_58.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA is explicitly used by the changed condition through MSSA->dominates(IMD, &MA).; The issue assertion concerns MemorySSA bookkeeping while removing an access that still has uses; this candidate changes which MemorySSA accesses LICM considers when deciding whether to move an instruction.
Reproducer link: The candidate changes LICM behavior under loop-mssa, a transformation that can run in optimized pipelines and move memory-writing calls out of loops.; The added tests specifically exercise hoisting decisions involving calls with inaccessible-memory effects and memory-ordering conflicts, but they do not show the reported assertion or the reduced C testcase.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; loop-mssa; MemorySSA
Causal explanation: This is a plausible bisect candidate because it directly alters a MemorySSA-dependent LICM decision that changes whether memory-affecting instructions are hoisted. Such movement requires correct MemorySSA maintenance and can expose inconsistent use/def bookkeeping. The retrieved change does not itself call removeFromLookups or show an updater/removal operation, so the link to the exact assertion is indirect rather than conclusive.
Causal confidence: 0.62
Build risk: The implementation change is small and localized to LICM's MemorySSA-based conflict scan.; A new regression test explicitly runs opt with loop-mssa(licm), providing direct test coverage of the changed path.; Changing which accesses are skipped can broaden LICM hoisting opportunities, increasing regression risk in MemorySSA update and preservation paths.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..03ab270de12e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/hoist-inaccesiblemem-call.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,163 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(licm)' < %s -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; It should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; because there is no conflict between inaccessible memory
+;; fn_read_inaccessible_mem is a nice side effect
+define i32 @loop_alias(i64 %x, ptr %start) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @loop_alias(
+; CHECK-SAME: i64 [[X:%.*]], ptr [[START:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_args(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_args(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %load)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}
+
+;; It should NOT hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; Because fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2 reads the same inaccessible memory
+define i32 @ne_loop_alias(i64 %x, ptr %start) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i32 @ne_loop_alias(
+; CHECK-SAME: i64 [[X:%.*]], ptr [[START:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ [[START]], %[[ENTRY]] ], [ [[GEP:%.*]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LOAD:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[PHI]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 [[LOAD]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 [[VAL]])
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP]] = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr [[PHI]], i64 [[X]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC:%.*]] = add nuw nsw i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP:%.*]] = icmp ult i32 [[ACC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_read_inaccessible_mem_2(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %val)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x
+  %acc = add nuw nsw i32 %val, 1
+  %cmp = icmp ult i32 %acc, 10
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %after_loop
+after_loop:
+  ret i32 %acc
+}
+
+;; Should hoist fn_write_inaccessible_mem
+;; It does not alias with store
+define void @hoist_untill_I(ptr noalias %loc, ptr noalias %loc2){
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @hoist_untill_I(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr noalias [[LOC:%.*]], ptr noalias [[LOC2:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[LOC2]], align 4
+; CHECK-N

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM revert restores a MemorySSA-based safety check in store-hoisting conflict analysis. It prevents non-sinking store hoists when the candidate instruction's MemorySSA definition does not dominate a relevant MemoryUse, addressing cases where an optimized clobber result points outside the loop because MemorySSA examines a prior loop iteration along the backedge.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; LICMPass::run; LNICMPass::run; load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def
Behavioral change: LICM now rejects a non-sinking store hoist when !MSSA->dominates(IMD, MU).; The restored condition accounts for optimized MemorySSA uses whose clobber may be outside the loop due to backedge/previous-iteration traversal.; A new LICM regression test verifies that a store is not hoisted past a preceding potentially interfering load when the load's clobber is liveOnEntry.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; optimized Uses; getClobbering
Reproducer link: The added loop testcase has a preceding load and a store to @g1; its backedge pointer can select @g2, causing the load's clobber to be liveOnEntry while the load can still interfere with the store.; The issue occurs under -O3 in optimizer memory-access bookkeeping, and LICM store hoisting is an O3 loop transformation that changes memory accesses.
Pass or subsystem link: LICM; MemorySSA; Scalar optimizer
Causal explanation: This is the strongest candidate-level match. The change explicitly guards a MemorySSA-use/dominance relationship during a transformation that moves stores. The issue assertion says MemorySSA is removing an access that still has uses; permitting an unsafe store hoist in the documented outside-loop-clobber case could leave MemorySSA users inconsistent during subsequent updates. Although the visible hunk does not show removeFromLookups itself, it restores a check specifically motivated by optimized MemorySSA uses.
Causal confidence: 0.82

selected_hunks.patch:
diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/store-hoisting.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/store-hoisting.ll
index a746caec18e5..207a1831bb6e 100644
--- a/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/store-hoisting.ll
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LICM/store-hoisting.ll
@@ -691,0 +692,35 @@ exit:
+
+@g1 = external global i8
+@g2 = external global i8
+
+; The store should not be hoisted here, because the location is accessed by the
+; preceding load. However, the clobbering memory access for that load is
+; liveOnEntry, because the pointer on the backedge does not alias. As such,
+; only checking whether the clobbering access is outside the loop is
+; insufficient.
+define i8 @load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def(i1 %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i8 @load_before_store_with_out_of_loop_def(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[C:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PHI:%.*]] = phi ptr [ @g1, %[[ENTRY]] ], [ @g2, %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = load i8, ptr [[PHI]], align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i8 1, ptr @g1, align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i8 [ [[V]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i8 [[V_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ @g1, %entry ], [ @g2, %loop ]
+  %v = load i8, ptr %phi
+  store i8 1, ptr @g1
+  br i1 %c, label %loop, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret i8 %v
+}

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This SROA change routes SROAPass options into the SROA implementation and adds coverage for opt-in homogeneous-aggregate-to-vector canonicalization. The new tests specifically exercise struct allocas, memcpy/memset chains, vector partitioning, and the default O3 phase ordering that delays struct-to-vector canonicalization until after memcpy optimization.
Changed symbols: SROAPass::run; SROA::runSROA; selectPartitionType; store_only_fp_tail; foo_flat; move_then_swap
Behavioral change: SROAPass::run now constructs SROA with the complete Options object rather than only the PreserveCFG value, allowing SROA behavior to depend on options such as AggregateToVector.; selectPartitionType now records selection decisions for direct fixed-vector types, integer fallback, byte-array fallback, and common-type selection through LogSelection; the shown selection predicates themselves are not materially changed.; New tests require aggregate-to-vector SROA mode to turn suitable homogeneous struct partitions into fixed vectors.; The added default<O3> phase-ordering test expects struct-to-vector canonicalization to occur after memcpyopt, permitting memcpyopt to collapse a memcpy/swap sequence into load, memmove, and store operations.
Assertion or trace link: No direct MemorySSA::removeFromLookups or "still has uses" assertion text appears in the retrieved hunks.; The change operates on allocas, memcpy, memset, loads, and stores, which are memory-access-producing IR operations relevant to MemorySSA bookkeeping.
Reproducer link: The new PhaseOrdering test explicitly runs opt -passes='default<O3>'.; The covered patterns contain memcpy/memset chains, aggregate allocas, and later load/store or vector-store rewrites, but no crash or assertion reproducer is shown.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e98c9074e4f8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -S -passes='default<O3>' %s | FileCheck %s
+
+%pair = type { i64, i64 }
+%quad = type { i64, i64, i64, i64 }
+
+declare void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr noalias writeonly captures(none), ptr noalias readonly captures(none), i64, i1 immarg)
+declare void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr writeonly captures(none), i8, i64, i1 immarg)
+
+; This test verifies that the default O3 pipeline canonicalizes struct allocas
+; to vectors only after memcpyopt has run. The input pattern is:
+;
+;   memcpy tmp, obj, 16
+;   memset obj + 16, 0, 16
+;
+;  ----- SWAP(other, tmp) -----
+;
+;   memcpy swap.tmp, tmp, 16
+;   memcpy tmp, other, 16
+;   memcpy other, swap.tmp, 16
+;
+; It swaps the first 16-bytes of other and tmp, but the first 16-bytes of tmp
+; are the same as the first 16-bytes of obj. This comes from real code from
+; DuckDB, where the swap function is inlined. If struct-to-vector canonicalization
+; runs before memcpyopt, swap.tmp gets promoted to an SSA value and we are stuck
+; saving tmp to swap.tmp. Delaying canonicalization until after memcpyopt lets
+; memcpyopt notice that tmp and obj share the same first 16-bytes, so swap.tmp
+; is no longer needed and the IR collapses to a single load/memmove/store.
+define void @move_then_swap(ptr %dst, ptr %src, ptr %other) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @move_then_swap(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr writeonly captures(none) initializes((0, 16)) [[DST:%.*]], ptr readonly captures(none) [[SRC:%.*]], ptr captures(none) [[OTHER:%.*]]) local_unnamed_addr #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD:%.*]] = load <2 x i64>, ptr [[OTHER]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    tail call void @llvm.memmove.p0.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[OTHER]], ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[SRC]], i64 16, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store <2 x i64> [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD]], ptr [[DST]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  %obj = alloca %quad, align 8
+  %swap.tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %obj, i64 16, i1 false)
+  %obj.tail = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %obj, i64 16
+  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj.tail, i8 0, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %other, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %other, ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..e98c9074e4f8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/struct-to-vector-before-memcpyopt.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -S -passes='default<O3>' %s | FileCheck %s
+
+%pair = type { i64, i64 }
+%quad = type { i64, i64, i64, i64 }
+
+declare void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr noalias writeonly captures(none), ptr noalias readonly captures(none), i64, i1 immarg)
+declare void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr writeonly captures(none), i8, i64, i1 immarg)
+
+; This test verifies that the default O3 pipeline canonicalizes struct allocas
+; to vectors only after memcpyopt has run. The input pattern is:
+;
+;   memcpy tmp, obj, 16
+;   memset obj + 16, 0, 16
+;
+;  ----- SWAP(other, tmp) -----
+;
+;   memcpy swap.tmp, tmp, 16
+;   memcpy tmp, other, 16
+;   memcpy other, swap.tmp, 16
+;
+; It swaps the first 16-bytes of other and tmp, but the first 16-bytes of tmp
+; are the same as the first 16-bytes of obj. This comes from real code from
+; DuckDB, where the swap function is inlined. If struct-to-vector canonicalization
+; runs before memcpyopt, swap.tmp gets promoted to an SSA value and we are stuck
+; saving tmp to swap.tmp. Delaying canonicalization until after memcpyopt lets
+; memcpyopt notice that tmp and obj share the same first 16-bytes, so swap.tmp
+; is no longer needed and the IR collapses to a single load/memmove/store.
+define void @move_then_swap(ptr %dst, ptr %src, ptr %other) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @move_then_swap(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr writeonly captures(none) initializes((0, 16)) [[DST:%.*]], ptr readonly captures(none) [[SRC:%.*]], ptr captures(none) [[OTHER:%.*]]) local_unnamed_addr #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD:%.*]] = load <2 x i64>, ptr [[OTHER]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    tail call void @llvm.memmove.p0.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[OTHER]], ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(16) [[SRC]], i64 16, i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store <2 x i64> [[TMP_SROA_0_0_COPYLOAD]], ptr [[DST]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  %obj = alloca %quad, align 8
+  %swap.tmp = alloca %pair, align 8
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj, ptr align 8 %src, i64 32, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %obj, i64 16, i1 false)
+  %obj.tail = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %obj, i64 16
+  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %obj.tail, i8 0, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %tmp, ptr align 8 %other, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %other, ptr align 8 %swap.tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 8 %dst, ptr align 8 %tmp, i64 16, i1 false)
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change adds a MemorySSA-backed path to GVN redundant-load elimination. When the MemorySSA mode is enabled, GVN derives reaching memory values from MemorySSA, queries MemorySSA walkers for clobbers when deciding whether loads may be hoisted, and uses those results for local and nonlocal load availability instead of relying solely on MemoryDependenceAnalysis.
Changed symbols: GVNPass::processLoad; GVNPass::findLoadToHoistIntoPred; GVNPass::AnalyzeLoadAvailability; GVNPass::scanMemoryAccessesUsers; GVNPass::findReachingValuesForLoad; GVNPass::ReachingMemVal; ValueTable::addMemoryStateToExp; findInvariantGroupValue
Behavioral change: GVN now conditionally uses MemorySSA to find reaching memory values for loads; if the search finds multiple predecessors or a nonlocal reaching value, it passes those values into nonlocal-load processing.; GVN load-hoisting checks can obtain a MemoryUse and its clobbering MemoryAccess through the MemorySSA walker rather than using MemDep locality alone.; Load-availability analysis uses ReachingMemVal block, address, and offset information, with MemorySSA-specific validation of coercible clobbering loads.; A hidden gvn-scan-users-limit option bounds the number of memory accesses scanned during reaching-memory-value analysis.; The retrieved option context shows enable-gvn-memoryssa defaults to false, so this new path is not demonstrated as enabled by default.
Assertion or trace link: Directly matches the issue subsystem through MemorySSA, MemoryAccess, MemoryUse, and MemorySSA walker operations.; No retrieved hunk mentions MemorySSA::removeFromLookups or the exact diagnostic "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses."
Reproducer link: The affected behavior is GVN load elimination and hoisting when the MemorySSA mode is enabled.; No reduced C testcase, default<O3> pipeline invocation, or proof that O3 enables this option is present in the retrieved evidence.
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; MemorySSA; MemorySSA walker; scalar load elimination and load PRE
Causal explanation: This is the strongest direct subsystem match: GVN becomes a new or substantially expanded MemorySSA consumer and makes transformation decisions from MemoryAccess and clobber queries. A GVN transformation that removes or replaces memory instructions must keep the associated MemorySSA state valid, making this relevant to an assertion about removing an access that still has uses. The visible code does not show a faulty updater call, and the MemorySSA mode defaults to false in the shown context, so causation for an ordinary -O3 crash remains unproven.

steps.subject: [LSR] Keep ICmpZero comparisons in integer domain to avoid inttoptr casts (#201970)

evidence: Changes LSR expansion of pointer-based ICmpZero uses in loops containing loads and stores.
It can alter O3 loop IR and downstream optimizer input, but it has no visible MemorySSA, updater, or memory-access deletion mechanism.
features: indirect_loop_ir_change, loop_strength_reduction, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar, path:llvm/test/CodeGen/X86, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes Loop Strength Reduction expansion for pointer-based zero comparisons. In LSRInstance::Expand, an LSRUse::ICmpZero whose operand type is a pointer is now expanded using ScalarEvolution's effective SCEV integer type rather than the pointer type, so the comparison remains in the integer domain and LSR avoids materializing inttoptr casts. The added X86 regression test verifies this on a loop containing loads and a store.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::Expand; LSRUse::ICmpZero; test_no_inttoptr_casts
Behavioral change: For pointer-typed ICmpZero uses, LSR replaces the expansion type with SE.getEffectiveSCEVType(OpTy).; LSR emits integer induction-variable comparisons against integer bounds instead of reconstructing pointer values with inttoptr casts.; The transformed loop still contains memory operations, but its pointer/value-def structure and generated comparison instructions differ.
Reproducer link: The new regression is a loop with multiple pointer induction variables, two loads, and a store; it does not show the PR204589 reduced testcase or a MemorySSA failure.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; ScalarEvolution; scalar loop optimization
Causal explanation: This is an optimizer change that rewrites loop IR containing memory operations, so it could indirectly alter the instruction/value graph presented to later MemorySSA users at -O3. However, the retrieved implementation does not reference MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, removeFromLookups, access removal, or use replacement. The direct change is limited to choosing an integer expansion type for pointer ICmpZero comparisons, making the connection to the reported "still has uses" MemorySSA assertion indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Adds a targeted opt/FileCheck regression test for loop-reduce on x86_64.; The test explicitly relies on target-dependent TTI legality for scaled addressing.; No MemorySSA-specific regression or implementation change is present in the retrieved candidate hunks.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0d6a374f8669
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-reduce -S %s | FileCheck %s
+;
+; Verify that LSR keeps ICmpZero comparisons in the integer domain when the
+; original operands are pointers, avoiding inttoptr casts entirely. The loop
+; has three pointer IVs sharing the same stride; LSR should produce a single
+; integer IV and compare it directly against the precomputed bound.
+; Target-dependent because TTI must report that scaled addressing is legal.
+
+target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+target datalayout = "e-m:e-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
+
+define void @test_no_inttoptr_casts(ptr %base1, ptr %base2, ptr %base3, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @test_no_inttoptr_casts(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = shl i64 [[N:%.*]], 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ], [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE1:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP1:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE2:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP2:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE3:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_EXIT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_EXIT]], label [[CHECK:%.*]], label [[BODY:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       check:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP3:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i1 true, i1 [[CMP3]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[SEL]], label [[BODY]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V1:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V2:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP1]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUM:%.*]] = add i64 [[V1]], [[V2]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SUM]], ptr [[SCEVGEP2]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %bound1 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base1, i64 %n
+  %bound2 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base2, i64 %n
+  %bound3 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base3, i64 %n
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %p1 = phi ptr [ %base1, %entry ], [ %p1.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p2 = phi ptr [ %base2, %entry ], [ %p2.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p3 = phi ptr [ %base3, %entry ], [ %p3.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %cmp.exit = icmp eq ptr %p2, %bound2
+  br i1 %cmp.exit, label %check, label %body
+
+check:
+  %cmp1 = icmp ne ptr %p1, %bound1
+  %cmp3 = icmp ne ptr %p3, %bound3
+  %sel = select i1 %cmp1, i1 true, i1 %cmp3
+  br i1 %sel, label %body, label %exit
+
+body:
+  %v1 = load i64, ptr %p1, align 8
+  %v2 = load i64, ptr %p2, align 8
+  %sum = add i64 %v1, %v2
+  store i64 %sum, ptr %p3, align 8
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+loop.latch:
+  %p1.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p1, i64 8
+  %p2.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p2, i64 8
+  %p3.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p3, i64 8
+  br label %loop
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.subject: [LSR] Keep ICmpZero comparisons in integer domain to avoid inttoptr casts (#201970)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes Loop Strength Reduction expansion for pointer-based zero comparisons. In LSRInstance::Expand, an LSRUse::ICmpZero whose operand type is a pointer is now expanded using ScalarEvolution's effective SCEV integer type rather than the pointer type, so the comparison remains in the integer domain and LSR avoids materializing inttoptr casts. The added X86 regression test verifies this on a loop containing loads and a store.
Changed symbols: LSRInstance::Expand; LSRUse::ICmpZero; test_no_inttoptr_casts
Behavioral change: For pointer-typed ICmpZero uses, LSR replaces the expansion type with SE.getEffectiveSCEVType(OpTy).; LSR emits integer induction-variable comparisons against integer bounds instead of reconstructing pointer values with inttoptr casts.; The transformed loop still contains memory operations, but its pointer/value-def structure and generated comparison instructions differ.
Reproducer link: The new regression is a loop with multiple pointer induction variables, two loads, and a store; it does not show the PR204589 reduced testcase or a MemorySSA failure.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopStrengthReduce; ScalarEvolution; scalar loop optimization
Causal explanation: This is an optimizer change that rewrites loop IR containing memory operations, so it could indirectly alter the instruction/value graph presented to later MemorySSA users at -O3. However, the retrieved implementation does not reference MemorySSA, MemorySSAUpdater, removeFromLookups, access removal, or use replacement. The direct change is limited to choosing an integer expansion type for pointer ICmpZero comparisons, making the connection to the reported "still has uses" MemorySSA assertion indirect.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Adds a targeted opt/FileCheck regression test for loop-reduce on x86_64.; The test explicitly relies on target-dependent TTI legality for scaled addressing.; No MemorySSA-specific regression or implementation change is present in the retrieved candidate hunks.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..0d6a374f8669
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopStrengthReduce/X86/lsr-icmpzero-no-inttoptr.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-reduce -S %s | FileCheck %s
+;
+; Verify that LSR keeps ICmpZero comparisons in the integer domain when the
+; original operands are pointers, avoiding inttoptr casts entirely. The loop
+; has three pointer IVs sharing the same stride; LSR should produce a single
+; integer IV and compare it directly against the precomputed bound.
+; Target-dependent because TTI must report that scaled addressing is legal.
+
+target triple = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+target datalayout = "e-m:e-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
+
+define void @test_no_inttoptr_casts(ptr %base1, ptr %base2, ptr %base3, i64 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @test_no_inttoptr_casts(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0:%.*]] = shl i64 [[N:%.*]], 3
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[LSR_IV_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ], [ 0, [[ENTRY:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE1:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP1:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE2:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SCEVGEP2:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[BASE3:%.*]], i64 [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_EXIT:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_EXIT]], label [[CHECK:%.*]], label [[BODY:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       check:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP3:%.*]] = icmp ne i64 [[TMP0]], [[LSR_IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i1 true, i1 [[CMP3]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[SEL]], label [[BODY]], label [[EXIT:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V1:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V2:%.*]] = load i64, ptr [[SCEVGEP1]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUM:%.*]] = add i64 [[V1]], [[V2]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SUM]], ptr [[SCEVGEP2]], align 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 8
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %bound1 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base1, i64 %n
+  %bound2 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base2, i64 %n
+  %bound3 = getelementptr i64, ptr %base3, i64 %n
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %p1 = phi ptr [ %base1, %entry ], [ %p1.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p2 = phi ptr [ %base2, %entry ], [ %p2.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %p3 = phi ptr [ %base3, %entry ], [ %p3.next, %loop.latch ]
+  %cmp.exit = icmp eq ptr %p2, %bound2
+  br i1 %cmp.exit, label %check, label %body
+
+check:
+  %cmp1 = icmp ne ptr %p1, %bound1
+  %cmp3 = icmp ne ptr %p3, %bound3
+  %sel = select i1 %cmp1, i1 true, i1 %cmp3
+  br i1 %sel, label %body, label %exit
+
+body:
+  %v1 = load i64, ptr %p1, align 8
+  %v2 = load i64, ptr %p2, align 8
+  %sum = add i64 %v1, %v2
+  store i64 %sum, ptr %p3, align 8
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+loop.latch:
+  %p1.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p1, i64 8
+  %p2.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p2, i64 8
+  %p3.next = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %p3, i64 8
+  br label %loop
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

Summary: This SLP Vectorizer change makes scalar intrinsic-call packs profitable when a vector library or vector intrinsic mapping is available, as reflected by updated tests. Summary: This commit is a cleanup that removes unused DenseMapInfo::getEmptyKey specializations and related sentinel handling from several scalar and utility components. The only behavioral-looking adjustment shown is that EarlyCSE's SimpleValue constructor now always requires a handleable instruction rather than allowing the DenseMap empty-key sentinel; the stated purpose and visible edits indicate removal of no-longer-used sentinel support rather than a transformation-algorithm change.
Changed symbols: llvm::DenseMapInfo<ModelledPHI>::getEmptyKey; llvm::DenseMapInfo<const EqualBBWrapper *>::getEmptyKey; EliminateDuplicatePHINodesSetBasedImpl::getEmptyKey; EliminateDuplicatePHINodesSetBasedImpl::isSentinel; SimpleValue::SimpleValue; SimpleValue::isSentinel; llvm::DenseMapInfo<const Expression *>::getEmptyKey; llvm::DenseMapInfo<FrozenIndPHIInfo>::getEmptyKey
Behavioral change: Removes unused DenseMap empty-key specializations for ModelledPHI, EqualBBWrapper, Expression, and FrozenIndPHIInfo.; Removes Local.cpp duplicate-PHI sentinel helpers.; Changes EarlyCSE SimpleValue construction to assert only canHandle(I), eliminating the prior empty-key sentinel exception.; No retrieved hunk changes memory-access creation, deletion, MemorySSA updates, or optimizer pass sequencing.
Assertion or trace link: No direct MemorySSA::removeFromLookups change or matching assertion text is present.; The only changed assertion is EarlyCSE SimpleValue's canHandle(I) assertion, which is distinct from the reported MemorySSA assertion.
Reproducer link: No reproducer for an -O3 crash, memory-access removal, or still-live MemorySSA uses is added or modified in the retrieved hunks.
Pass or subsystem link: Transforms/Scalar/EarlyCSE; Transforms/Scalar/GVNSink; Transforms/Scalar/NewGVN; Transforms/Utils/SimplifyCFG; Transforms/Utils/Local
Causal explanation: The commit touches scalar and CFG utility code, which places it in optimizer-adjacent territory, but every retrieved change is removal of unused DenseMap sentinel machinery. There is no evidence that these removals manipulate IR memory instructions or invoke MemorySSA maintenance. The altered EarlyCSE assertion could expose misuse of a removed sentinel if such misuse existed, but that is not the reported removeFromLookups assertion and is unsupported as a causal explanation by the retrieved hunks.
Causal confidence: 0.04

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes LoopInterchange legality to reject guarded imperfect loop nests: when an outer-loop header can bypass the inner loop and reach the outer latch, the nest is no longer considered tightly nested and is not interchanged. It updates LoopInterchange output checks and adds a regression test showing that interchanging a guarded inner loop can turn a terminating loop into a nonterminating one.
Changed symbols: LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested; LoopInterchange; lcssa_08; guarded-inner-loop.ll
Behavioral change: Tight-nesting legality now requires the outer header to branch only into the inner loop, rejecting nests whose inner loop is conditionally guarded by a path to the outer latch.; LoopInterchange no longer transforms guarded imperfect nests even when other interchange conditions may hold.; The added test requires a NotTightlyNested missed-optimization result for a guarded inner loop whose termination depends on the guard.
Assertion or trace link: No direct MemorySSA::removeFromLookups change or matching assertion text is present in the retrieved hunks.; No retrieved hunk mentions "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses" or MemorySSA.
Reproducer link: The new reproducer concerns an invalid/nonterminating loop interchange when an inner loop is skipped on guarded outer iterations.; The updated lcssa_08 checks cover changed loop CFG/LCSSA output after the interchange is rejected.
Pass or subsystem link: Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange; Loop CFG and LCSSA-form transformations
Causal explanation: This is a scalar loop-transform legality change that can materially alter CFG shape and whether loop interchange executes, which is broadly adjacent to optimizer memory-access bookkeeping. However, the retrieved implementation changes only the legality predicate and contains no MemorySSA update, MemorySSA user, memory-access deletion, or invalidation logic. The change prevents a transform rather than introducing a new mutation path, so the evidence for it causing the reported MemorySSA removal assertion is weak.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Implementation change in a scalar transformation pass.; Adds a focused loop-interchange regression test.; Updates FileCheck expectations for lcssa-preheader output, providing test coverage for the changed CFG behavior.

diff --git a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
index 28eef9c2790d..b2e3bbe516ed 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LoopInterchange.cpp
@@ -827,3 +827,18 @@ bool LoopInterchangeLegality::tightlyNested(Loop *OuterLoop, Loop *InnerLoop) {
-  // A perfectly nested loop will not have any branch in between the outer and
-  // inner block i.e. outer header will branch to either inner preheader and
-  // outerloop latch.
+  // In a perfectly nested loop the outer header branches only into the inner
+  // loop. If it can also reach the outer latch, it conditionally guards the
+  // inner loop (an imperfect nest), so the inner loop runs on only a subset of
+  // the outer iterations. Interchanging such a nest would run the inner loop on
+  // every outer iteration, including the guarded-off ones, which is illegal
+  // when the inner loop relies on the guard to terminate (e.g. an eq/ne exit
+  // whose trip count is degenerate once the guard is false). Reject by allowing
+  // the outer header to branch only into the inner loop.
+  //
+  // TODO: This is conservative. A guarded nest is still safe to interchange
+  // when the inner loop has a computable trip count that is empty exactly when
+  // the guard is false, e.g.:
+  //   for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
+  //     if (M > 0)                  // loop-invariant guard
+  //       for (j = 0; j < M; j++)   // empty when M <= 0
+  //         A[j][i] = ...;
+  // Interchanging is legal here because the inner loop runs zero times on the
+  // guarded-off iterations.

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..681dca5bbcba
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/guarded-inner-loop.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes=loop-interchange \
+; RUN:     -loop-interchange-profitabilities=ignore \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-missed='loop-interchange' -disable-output \
+; RUN:     -pass-remarks-output=%t
+; RUN: FileCheck -input-file=%t %s
+
+; The middle loop %for.j guards the inner loop %for.k: %for.k runs only when
+; %i != 0 (the outer loop's IV), and its exit %k.next == %i is only well-defined
+; under that guard. Interchanging %for.j and %for.k would run %for.k on every
+; iteration and spin when %i == 0, so the pass must not interchange this nest.
+;
+; Pseudo code:
+;   for (i = 0; i < 3; i++)
+;     for (j = 0; j < 2; j++)
+;       if (i != 0)                  // guard on the outer IV
+;         for (k = 0; ; k++) {       // terminates only when i != 0
+;           y[j][i][k] = x[i][k][j] + w[i][k][j];
+;           if (k + 1 == i) break;
+;         }
+
+; CHECK:      --- !Missed
+; CHECK-NEXT: Pass:            loop-interchange
+; CHECK-NEXT: Name:            NotTightlyNested
+; CHECK-NEXT: Function:        main
+
+@x = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@w = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+@y = global [3 x [3 x [3 x i32]]] zeroinitializer
+
+define i32 @main() {
+entry:
+  br label %for.i
+
+for.i:
+  %i = phi i32 [ %i.next, %for.i.inc ], [ 0, %entry ]
+  %i.is.zero = icmp eq i32 %i, 0
+  %xbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @x, i32 %i
+  %wbase = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr @w, i32 %i
+  %ybase = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr @y, i32 %i
+  br label %for.j
+
+for.j:
+  %j = phi i32 [ %j.next, %for.j.inc ], [ 0, %for.i ]
+  br i1 %i.is.zero, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k.ph
+
+for.k.ph:
+  %xp = getelementptr i32, ptr %xbase, i32 %j
+  %wp = getelementptr i32, ptr %wbase, i32 %j
+  %yp = getelementptr [9 x i32], ptr %ybase, i32 %j
+  br label %for.k
+
+for.k:
+  %k = phi i32 [ 0, %for.k.ph ], [ %k.next, %for.k ]
+  %xk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %xp, i32 %k
+  %xv = load i32, ptr %xk, align 4
+  %wk = getelementptr [3 x i32], ptr %wp, i32 %k
+  %wv = load i32, ptr %wk, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %xv, %wv
+  %yk = getelementptr i32, ptr %yp, i32 %k
+  store i32 %add, ptr %yk, align 4
+  %k.next = add i32 %k, 1
+  %k.done = icmp eq i32 %k.next, %i
+  br i1 %k.done, label %for.j.inc, label %for.k
+
+for.j.inc:
+  %j.next = add i32 %j, 1
+  %j.cmp = icmp eq i32 %j, 0
+  br i1 %j.cmp, label %for.j, label %for.i.inc
+
+for.i.inc:
+  %i.next = add i32 %i, 1
+  %i.done = icmp eq i32 %i.next, 3
+  br i1 %i.done, label %exit, label %for.i
+
+exit:
+  ret i32 0
+}

steps.subject: [VPlan] Simplify reverse(reverse(x)) -> x (#199057)

evidence: Changes VPlan simplification around reverse loads and stores, including masked and VP store forms.
The rewrite removes pure reverse operations rather than tracked memory accesses, leaving only an indirect MemorySSA connection.
features: loop-vectorize, masked-stores, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize, reverse-simplification
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: The candidate simplifies VPlan expressions of the form reverse(reverse(x)) to x. The new VPlan test constructs a reverse load followed by a reverse before a store, while updated LoopVectorize tests expect the redundant reverse instructions to disappear and the original loaded vector value to be stored directly, including VP and masked-store forms.
Changed symbols: VPlan simplifyReverses; reverse_copy; test_runtime_check_known_false_after_construction; reverse_load_store; reverse_load_store_masked
Behavioral change: Canonicalizes nested vector reverse operations by replacing reverse(reverse(x)) with x.; Eliminates redundant shufflevector, llvm.vector.reverse, and llvm.experimental.vp.reverse operations from affected vectorized loops.; Changes the value directly supplied to ordinary, masked, and VP stores without changing the shown underlying load/store topology.
Reproducer link: The affected test contexts exercise vectorized loads, stores, masked stores, and VP stores, but no supplied test reproduces a MemorySSA assertion or removal of a memory access with remaining uses.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; VP and masked vector memory operations
Causal explanation: This is a substantive vectorizer-plan rewrite that changes value-producing instructions around memory operations. Such rewrites can indirectly affect later optimizer behavior, but the visible simplification removes redundant pure reverse operations rather than deleting or replacing the loads/stores whose MemorySSA accesses would be tracked. No retrieved hunk touches MemorySSA or demonstrates stale MemorySSA uses, so the evidence for the specific removeFromLookups assertion is weak.
Causal confidence: 0.10
Build risk: The retrieved implementation-facing evidence is primarily new and updated LoopVectorize/VPlan tests.; The change affects vector IR expected for fixed-width, scalable, masked, and VP forms.; No retrieved MemorySSA-specific validation or implementation change establishes interaction with MemorySSA.

+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/simplify-reverse-reverse.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_analyze_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --filter-out-after "middle.block:" --version 6
+; RUN: opt -p loop-vectorize -force-vector-width=4 -disable-output -vplan-print-after=simplifyReverses %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+
+define void @reverse_copy(ptr noalias %src, ptr noalias %dst, i32 %n) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: VPlan for loop in 'reverse_copy'
+; CHECK:  VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Live-in vp<[[VP0:%[0-9]+]]> = VF
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Live-in vp<[[VP1:%[0-9]+]]> = VF * UF
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Live-in vp<[[VP2:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-trip-count
+; CHECK-NEXT:  vp<[[VP3:%[0-9]+]]> = original trip-count
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ir-bb<entry>:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    EMIT vp<[[VP3]]> = EXPAND SCEV ((-1 * (0 smin (-1 + %n)<nsw>)) + %n)
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  vector.ph:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    vp<[[VP4:%[0-9]+]]> = DERIVED-IV ir<%n> + vp<[[VP2]]> * ir<-1>
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): vector loop
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  <x1> vector loop: {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  vp<[[VP5:%[0-9]+]]> = CANONICAL-IV
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    vector.body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:      ir<%iv> = WIDEN-INDUCTION nsw ir<%n>, ir<-1>, vp<[[VP0]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP6:%[0-9]+]]> = DERIVED-IV ir<%n> + vp<[[VP5]]> * ir<-1>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP7:%[0-9]+]]> = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[VP6]]>, ir<-1>, vp<[[VP0]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      CLONE ir<%iv.next> = add nsw vp<[[VP7]]>, ir<-1>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      CLONE ir<%gep.src> = getelementptr ir<%src>, ir<%iv.next>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP8:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-end-pointer ir<%gep.src>, vp<[[VP0]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      WIDEN ir<%x> = load vp<[[VP8]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      EMIT vp<[[VP9:%[0-9]+]]> = reverse ir<%x>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      CLONE ir<%gep.dst> = getelementptr ir<%dst>, ir<%iv.next>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP10:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-end-pointer ir<%gep.dst>, vp<[[VP0]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      EMIT vp<[[VP11:%[0-9]+]]> = reverse vp<[[VP9]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      WIDEN store vp<[[VP10]]>, ir<%x>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      EMIT vp<%index.next> = add nuw vp<[[VP5]]>, vp<[[VP1]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      EMIT branch-on-count vp<%index.next>, vp<[[VP2]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:    No successors
+; CHECK-NEXT:  }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): middle.block
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  middle.block:
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+
+loop:
+  %iv = phi i32 [%n, %entry], [%iv.next, %loop]
+  %iv.next = add nsw i32 %iv, -1
+  %gep.src = getelementptr i32, ptr %src, i32 %iv.next
+  %x = load i32, ptr %gep.src
+  %gep.dst = getelementptr i32, ptr %dst, i32 %iv.next
+  store i32 %x, ptr %gep.dst
+  %ec = icmp sgt i32 %iv.next, 0
+  br i1 %ec, label %loop, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

+; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): vector loop
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  <x1> vector loop: {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  vp<[[VP5:%[0-9]+]]> = CANONICAL-IV
+; CHECK-EMPTY:

+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP7:%[0-9]+]]> = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[VP6]]>, ir<-1>, vp<[[VP0]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      CLONE ir<%iv.next> = add nsw vp<[[VP7]]>, ir<-1>

+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP8:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-end-pointer ir<%gep.src>, vp<[[VP0]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      WIDEN ir<%x> = load vp<[[VP8]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      EMIT vp<[[VP9:%[0-9]+]]> = reverse ir<%x>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      CLONE ir<%gep.dst> = getelementptr ir<%dst>, ir<%iv.next>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[VP10:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-end-pointer ir<%gep.dst>, vp<[[VP0]]>

+; CHECK-NEXT:      WIDEN store vp<[[VP10]]>, ir<%x>

+; CHECK-NEXT:    No successors

+; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): middle.block
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  middle.block:
+;
+entry:

+  %x = load i32, ptr %gep.src

+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK:      VPlan for loop in 'foo' [[BEFORE_OR_AFTER]] printFinalVPlan
+; CHECK-NEXT: VPlan 'Final VPlan for VF={4},UF={1}' {
+
+define void @foo(ptr %ptr, i64 %n) {
+entry:
+  br label %header
+
+header:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %header ]
+  %gep = getelementptr i64, ptr %ptr, i64 %iv
+  store i64 %iv, ptr %gep
+  %iv.next = add nsw i64 %iv, 1
+  %exitcond = icmp slt i64 %iv.next, %n
+  br i1 %exitcond, label %header, label %exit
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

Summary: The retrieved first-parent hunks are test-only updates for LoopVectorize cost-reporting tests. They add update_analyze_test_checks.py metadata and replace or remove hand-written cost-output checks in LoopVectorize AArch64, ARM, and WebAssembly tests. Consistent with the commit subject, the observable intended change is formatting of per-lane vectorization costs using APFloat; no MemorySSA implementation or memory-access-update code is present in the retrieved candidate hunks.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorize cost-analysis diagnostic checks; two_ints_same_op; two_ints_vary_op; three_ints
Behavioral change: Updates expected LoopVectorize cost-analysis output, including estimated cost-per-lane formatting.; Moves affected test assertions toward autogenerated analysis-check metadata.; Does not show a change to IR transformation logic, MemorySSA, or MemorySSA access/use removal invariants in the retrieved hunks.
Reproducer link: The shown test functions contain loads and stores in vectorizer cost-analysis tests, but the candidate changes only their expected diagnostic assertions.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize diagnostic and cost reporting

+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopInterchange/inner-preheader-multi-entry-phi.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-interchange -loop-interchange-profitabilities=ignore \
+; RUN:   -verify-dom-info -verify-loop-info -verify-loop-lcssa -S %s \
+; RUN:   | FileCheck %s
+
+; The outer header branches to the inner preheader via duplicate edges, giving
+; the preheader a PHI with two identical incoming entries. Interchange must
+; succeed: both entries carry the same value so the PHI can be safely removed.
+
+define void @multi_entry_phi(ptr noalias %A, i1 %c) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @multi_entry_phi(
+; CHECK-SAME: ptr noalias [[A:%.*]], i1 [[C:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PH:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER_PREHEADER:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i64 [ [[I_INC:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ], [ 0, %[[OUTER_HEADER_PREHEADER]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[INNER_SPLIT1:.*]], label %[[INNER_SPLIT1]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 0, %[[INNER_PH]] ], [ [[TMP0:%.*]], %[[INNER_SPLIT:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER_PREHEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_SPLIT1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[IDX:%.*]] = mul i64 [[J]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[OFF:%.*]] = add i64 [[IDX]], [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i64 [[OFF]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 0, ptr [[GEP]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_INC:%.*]] = add i64 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC_J:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[J_INC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP0]] = add i64 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[TMP0]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[TMP1]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_INC]] = add i64 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EC_I:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[I_INC]], 10
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EC_I]], label %[[INNER_SPLIT]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %i = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %i.inc, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %c, label %inner.ph, label %inner.ph
+
+inner.ph:
+  %p = phi i64 [ 42, %outer.header ], [ 42, %outer.header ]
+  br label %inner
+
+inner:
+  %j = phi i64 [ 0, %inner.ph ], [ %j.inc, %inner ]
+  %idx = mul i64 %j, 10
+  %off = add i64 %idx, %i
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %off
+  store i32 0, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %j.inc = add i64 %j, 1
+  %ec.j = icmp eq i64 %j.inc, 10
+  br i1 %ec.j, label %outer.latch, label %inner
+
+outer.latch:
+  %i.inc = add i64 %i, 1
+  %ec.i = icmp eq i64 %i.inc, 10
+  br i1 %ec.i, label %exit, label %outer.header
+
+exit:
+  ret void
+}

top_candidates.subject: [InstCombine] Fold X == Identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y) (#202748)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The commit extends `simplifyWithOpsReplaced` in InstructionSimplify so a min/max intrinsic whose substituted operand is its identity constant simplifies to the other operand. It preserves poison semantics by refusing the fold when poison-generating annotations cannot be dropped, or recording the intrinsic in `DropFlags` when they can. New InstCombine tests cover signed/unsigned min/max identity comparisons and select folds, including a negative wrong-bound case and range-attribute dropping.
Changed symbols: simplifyWithOpsReplaced; MinMaxIntrinsic; select_signed_max_smin; select_npos_umin; select_not_npos_umin; select_npos_umin_commuted; select_npos_wrong_bound_negative; select_npos_umin_drop_range
Behavioral change: When an operand replacement makes a `MinMaxIntrinsic` operand equal to its identity value, the simplifier returns the other min/max operand.; The fold is blocked for poison-generating intrinsics unless flag dropping is permitted; when permitted, the intrinsic is added to `DropFlags`.; InstCombine can consequently fold select patterns such as `X == identity ? Y : min/max(X, Y)` to the existing min/max result.
Assertion or trace link: No `MemorySSA`, `removeFromLookups`, or "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses" diagnostic is present in the retrieved hunks.
Reproducer link: The added reproducers contain integer `icmp`, `select`, and min/max intrinsics; they contain no loads, stores, allocas, or memory-access graph updates.
Pass or subsystem link: InstructionSimplify; InstCombine
Causal explanation: This is a scalar IR simplification that can change instruction use-def chains and remove selects/min/max operations, but the shown logic does not create, remove, or update memory accesses. It could only be related indirectly through changed IR presented to later `-O3` passes; the retrieved evidence provides no direct mechanism for violating MemorySSA's requirement that a removed access have no uses.
Causal confidence: 0.06
Build risk: Production implementation change is localized to InstructionSimplify and is covered by multiple InstCombine regression tests.; Poison-generating annotations and range attributes are explicitly exercised, so semantic-regression risk is concentrated in poison/flag handling.; No direct MemorySSA API, analysis-preservation, or memory-access mutation is touched in the retrieved evidence.

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: The retrieved first-parent evidence adds and updates InstCombine and phase-ordering tests for canonicalizing alignment operand bundles on llvm.assume calls. The expected behavior is to move an alignment assumption from a GEP result to its base pointer when the GEP offset preserves the stated alignment, while retaining the GEP-based assumption when alignment is not preserved or target pointer/index-width cases prevent the rewrite.
Changed symbols: align_on_i128_offset; align_on_i128_offset_unaligned; align_on_gep_keeping_alignment; align_on_gep_not_keeping_alignment; earlycse_entry; f1
Behavioral change: InstCombine test expectations canonicalize an align operand bundle on a GEP to the GEP base when the GEP's offset preserves the asserted alignment.; Tests retain the alignment bundle on the GEP when the offset may not preserve alignment.; Adds coverage for unusual pointer/index widths and large i128 GEP offsets, including cases where the GEP must remain.; Updates a phase-ordering expectation to refer to the canonicalized pointer used by an alignment assumption.
Pass or subsystem link: InstCombine; llvm.assume alignment operand-bundle canonicalization; PhaseOrdering
Causal explanation: This is the only candidate whose retrieved evidence describes an optimizer IR canonicalization that can eliminate or retarget a GEP and an associated assume. Such IR mutation could indirectly affect later optimization bookkeeping at -O3, but the shown changes concern alignment assumptions rather than memory accesses themselves. No retrieved first-parent hunk updates MemorySSA or shows the removeFromLookups/still-has-uses assertion, so the causal link remains weak.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Retrieved first-parent evidence is test-focused; no corresponding production InstCombine implementation hunk is available here.; Coverage includes non-default 16-bit and 128-bit pointer data layouts and large i128 GEP offsets, which makes test behavior sensitive to pointer-index canonicalization.; A PhaseOrdering expected-output change indicates potential pipeline-order sensitivity, but does not establish a MemorySSA failure.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: According to the commit subject and first-parent test updates, this change broadens SimpleLoopUnswitch's definition of a trivially unswitchable invariant branch. The new tests specify that an invariant guard which branches to an outer-loop latch can be converted into an exit-like edge and hoisted without duplicating the loop, while genuinely non-trivial unswitching that would duplicate a loop remains suppressed for cold size-optimized functions. The retrieved first-parent evidence is test-only, but it directly exercises the loop-mssa SimpleLoopUnswitch pipeline and changes expected loop CFGs containing loads and stores.
Changed symbols: SimpleLoopUnswitch; unswitchTrivialBranch; perfect_nest_guard; _Z7computeRSt6vectorIiSaIiEEy; _Z11hotFunctionbiiPiS_S_; function
Behavioral change: Treats a loop-invariant guard whose in-loop successor is the loop latch as eligible for trivial unswitching after rewriting the latch arm toward the outer-loop exit.; Hoists such guards out of a perfect outer loop without requiring full loop-body duplication.; Keeps non-trivial loop unswitching, which would duplicate the loop body, disabled for cold optsize/minsize functions.; Changes O3 and PGO phase-ordering CFG expectations for nested loops with memory loads and stores.

Such rewrites can require MemorySSA access replacement/removal and use-list maintenance, which is directly relevant to an assertion that an access is removed while still having uses. diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;

index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader

+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

Summary: According to the commit subject and first-parent test updates, this change broadens SimpleLoopUnswitch's definition of a trivially unswitchable invariant branch. The new tests specify that an invariant guard which branches to an outer-loop latch can be converted into an exit-like edge and hoisted without duplicating the loop, while genuinely non-trivial unswitching that would duplicate a loop remains suppressed for cold size-optimized functions. The retrieved first-parent evidence is test-only, but it directly exercises the loop-mssa SimpleLoopUnswitch pipeline and changes expected loop CFGs containing loads and stores.
Changed symbols: SimpleLoopUnswitch; unswitchTrivialBranch; perfect_nest_guard; _Z7computeRSt6vectorIiSaIiEEy; _Z11hotFunctionbiiPiS_S_; function
Behavioral change: Treats a loop-invariant guard whose in-loop successor is the loop latch as eligible for trivial unswitching after rewriting the latch arm toward the outer-loop exit.; Hoists such guards out of a perfect outer loop without requiring full loop-body duplication.; Keeps non-trivial loop unswitching, which would duplicate the loop body, disabled for cold optsize/minsize functions.; Changes O3 and PGO phase-ordering CFG expectations for nested loops with memory loads and stores.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes `llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest` in SimplifyCFG so speculative-execution safety is evaluated in the context of the sole predecessor's terminator and its `AssumptionCache`. It extends the helper signature with `AssumptionCache *AC`, passes `Options.AC` from `SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch`, and calls `isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute(&I, CxtI, AC)`. The added tests show branch folding may now speculate a dereferenceable load into the predecessor when dereferenceability is available from an argument attribute or a constant-size `llvm.assume`, while a variable-size dereferenceable assumption remains unhoisted in the shown test.
Changed symbols: llvm::foldBranchToCommonDest; SimplifyCFGOpt::simplifyCondBranch; isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute; AssumptionCache; load_derefable; load_derefable_assume; load_derefable_assume_var
Behavioral change: Supplies a contextual instruction and AssumptionCache when deciding whether instructions from a branch can be safely speculated into its predecessor.; Limits the context-instruction case to a single predecessor, using that predecessor's terminator as the insertion context.; Allows SimplifyCFG to fold selected branch shapes by moving dereferenceable loads before the predecessor branch when assumptions prove the speculation safe.; Does not directly alter `MemorySSA::removeFromLookups`, MemorySSA use lists, or the visible `MemorySSAUpdater` handling; the shown `simplifyCondBranch` call still passes `MSSAU=nullptr`.
Assertion or trace link: No direct change to `MemorySSA::removeFromLookups` or its "Trying to remove memory access that still has uses" assertion is present.; `isSafeToSpeculativelyExecute` is changed for loads, which can alter the set and placement of memory instructions processed by later optimization bookkeeping.
Reproducer link: The new tests specifically create conditional paths containing loads and cause some loads to be speculated into a predecessor under dereferenceability facts.; No retrieved hunk establishes that the reported reduced C testcase reaches this SimplifyCFG transformation or reproduces the assertion.
Pass or subsystem link: SimplifyCFG; Transforms/Utils; AssumptionCache; speculative load motion
Causal explanation: This is an indirect but plausible candidate: it changes which memory-reading instructions SimplifyCFG moves or deletes, thereby potentially changing inputs to existing MemorySSA-maintenance paths in callers that maintain MemorySSA. top_candidates.subject: [ConstraintElim] Do not model negative nuw-only GEP offset as signed. (#203620)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: ConstraintElimination now refuses to decompose a GEP with a negative constant offset when the GEP is nuw-only, because such an offset must be interpreted under unsigned rather than signed semantics. The corresponding regression expectation changes from an incorrect constant-true result to retaining an unsigned pointer comparison.
Changed symbols: decomposeGEP; GEPNoWrapFlags::hasNoUnsignedSignedWrap; ConstantOffset; gep_nuw_negative_offset_unsigned
Behavioral change: decomposeGEP returns the original GEP rather than constructing a signed decomposition when the GEP lacks nusw/inbounds semantics and its collected constant offset is negative.; ConstraintElimination no longer incorrectly simplifies the covered nuw-only negative-offset pointer predicate to true.; The regression test now expects an icmp ult between the derived pointer and its base pointer instead of ret i1 true.
Assertion or trace link: No MemorySSA::removeFromLookups assertion, 'Trying to remove memory access that still has uses' diagnostic, or MemorySSA.cpp reference appears in the retrieved implementation or test hunks.
Reproducer link: The reproduced behavior is an incorrect ConstraintElimination simplification of a pointer comparison involving a nuw-only negative GEP offset, not a Clang -O3 crash during MemorySSA updating.
Pass or subsystem link: ConstraintElimination; LLVM scalar optimizer; GEP no-wrap and pointer-comparison reasoning
Causal explanation: This is a scalar-optimizer change and can affect optimized IR at -O3, making it broadly adjacent to the issue area. However, the visible change only restricts symbolic GEP decomposition for correctness; it does not create, remove, move, or update memory accesses, and no MemorySSA interaction is shown. The retrieved evidence therefore supports only a weak indirect connection.
